purpose: Define when ordering is semantically meaningful in canonical data and prohibit accidental semantics from JSON array order, filesystem order, Topic order, projection order or renderer position.

value.name: Validate absence of accidental ordering semantics

value.default_rule: Collection order is non-semantic unless the owning Contract Format/type/field semantics explicitly declare ordering.
value.ordered_collection_rule: If order carries meaning, that meaning must be explicit and reproducible independently of incidental JSON array position.
value.unordered_collection_rule: Reordering an unordered collection does not change canonical semantic meaning.
value.execution_rule: Execution order exists only through explicit behavior.flows and their causal/continuation fields, never through ordinary array position.
value.topic_rule: Order of Topics, child_topics, parent_topic_refs or composed_topic_refs does not imply priority, execution order, ownership strength or semantic precedence.
value.structure_rule: Order of containment, relation, ownership, authority or dependency records does not alter their semantics.
value.reference_rule: Order of references does not imply precedence unless a separate owning semantic rule explicitly defines such precedence.
value.filesystem_rule: Directory enumeration, lexical filename order and numeric filename prefixes are storage/navigation conveniences only unless an explicit bootstrap/source rule says otherwise.
value.projection_rule: Sorting, layout, z-order, graph position or rendered sequence are projection semantics only and never feed back into canonical ordering.
value.deterministic_output_rule: A serializer/projector may choose a stable sort for reproducible output, but stable output order must not be mistaken for semantic order.

value.purpose: Group explicit ordering semantics and non-ordering guarantees for canonical collections and flows.

invariants.rule: Any semantically meaningful ordering is explicitly represented by its owning semantic model.
Reordering an unordered canonical collection preserves semantic equivalence.

hard_gates.condition: Execution order is inferred from ordinary JSON array position.
Topic list order is interpreted as priority, authority, execution order or semantic precedence.
Filename prefix or filesystem enumeration order is used as semantic ordering without an explicit owning rule.
Projection/render order is fed back as canonical ordering semantics.
A collection claims semantic order but provides no deterministic explicit ordering semantics.

references.purpose: Execution order and causal continuation are represented in explicit flows.
Normalization may reorder unordered collections without semantic change.
Projection ordering remains derived presentation semantics.

Pass 8 formalized previously free Flow actor/data/target/condition/payload/result/error tokens as exact owner-scoped member identities while preserving every source literal.

semantics.identity_rule: This member gives an exact owner-scoped identity to the literal Flow token without adding semantics beyond the owning Flow reference field and the preserved source literal.
semantics.interpretation_rule: Consumers may use this identity as an opaque declared Flow symbol. No meaning may be inferred from spelling, whitespace, filename, path or similarity to another symbol.
semantics.authority_rule: A Flow symbol is descriptive/causal model data only and never grants runtime authority, capability, ownership or execution permission.
semantics.scope_rule: Identity is scoped semantically to the defining contract; identical source literals in another contract or another Flow-ref role are not automatically the same semantic identity.
